key_insight: Travelling wall deformations drive particle transport whose direction depends on wave intensity, flow regime, and wall-material motion—not just the travelling shape.
engineering_relevance: Controlling radial and tangential wall motion could tune or reverse particle transport in deformable cavities.
method: Combine Eulerian mean flow and Stokes drift to obtain total Lagrangian drift.
Derive closed-form viscous-limit profiles and quadrature solutions at finite Womersley number.
Analyze high-frequency near-wall behavior and validate with moving-domain simulations.
evidence_signal: At azimuthal order m=2 and Wo²=10, moving-domain simulations recover leading-order drift coefficients for both radial-only and locally arc-length-preserving wall motions.
watch_item: Predictions are leading-order in wall amplitude; finite-amplitude performance and broader simulation validation are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Lagrangian transport driven by travelling waves in a radially deforming circular cavity
